[[File:Infinite lattice of divisors.svg|thumb|The non-negative integers partially ordered by divisibility.]]
The '''division lattice''' is an infinite complete bounded [[distributive lattice]] whose elements are the [[natural numbers]] ordered by [[divisibility]].  Its least element is 1, which divides all natural numbers, while its greatest element is 0, which is divisible by all positive natural numbers.  The meet operation is [[greatest common divisor]] while the join operation is [[least common multiple]].<ref>{{Citation | last1=Davey | first1=B. A. | last2=Priestley | first2=H. A. | title=Introduction to Lattices and Order|title-link= Introduction to Lattices and Order | publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] | isbn=978-0-521-78451-1 | year=2002|page=37}}</ref>

The [[prime numbers]] are precisely the [[atom (order theory)|atoms]] of the division lattice, namely those natural numbers divisible only by themselves and 1.<ref>{{citation|title=Groups, Rings And Modules With Applications|first1=M. R.|last1=Adhikari|first2=A.|last2=Adhikari|publisher=Universities Press|year=2003|isbn=9788173714290|page=13|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=oDkEWKi1ekwC&pg=PA13}}</ref>

For any [[square-free]] number ''n'', its divisors form a [[Boolean algebra]] that is a [[sublattice]] of the division lattice. The elements of this sublattice are representable as the subsets of the set of prime factors of ''n''. <ref>{{citation|title=Lectures on Boolean Algebras|series=Dover Books on Mathematics|first=Paul R.|last=Halmos|publisher=Courier Dover Publications|year=2018|isbn=9780486834573|page=7|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=izJnDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA7}}</ref>
